title: Best personal loans in Nigeria (2026)
intro: Personal loans in Nigeria range from instant app-based credit of a few thousand naira to multi-million-naira salary loans repaid over three years. The right choice depends on how fast you need the money, whether you bank where you're borrowing, and — above all — the true cost once management fees and monthly interest are added in. Headline 'monthly interest' figures can look small but compound into very high annual rates, so we convert every product to a comparable basis and show the fees alongside the rate. We list only products from institutions licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria, and we mark which providers have been licence-checked and have claimed their listing. Use the filters to sort by interest rate, fees or loan amount, and always confirm the exact terms with the provider before you apply — the figures here are indicative and change frequently.

faq.question: How were these personal loans ranked?
faq.answer: By default we sort by customer rating, with sponsored placements clearly labelled and shown first. You can re-sort by lowest interest, lowest fees or smallest minimum amount. Ranking never affects whether a provider is shown as licence-verified — that is a separate, factual check against the CBN register.

faq.question: What does the gold Verified badge mean?
faq.answer: It means the provider has been matched to the Central Bank of Nigeria's register of licensed institutions AND has claimed and confirmed its listing with us. Unlicensed or unclaimed lenders never receive the gold badge, even if they are popular.

faq.question: Are these interest rates and fees guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. All rates, fees and terms shown are indicative only and can change at any time. Each product shows the date we last verified its figures. Always confirm the exact terms directly with the provider before applying.

faq.question: What do I usually need to apply for a personal loan in Nigeria?
faq.answer: Most lenders require your Bank Verification Number (BVN) and a valid ID. Salary loans typically also need recent bank statements and proof of employment. Each product page lists the specific required documents.

faq.question: How can I reduce the cost of a personal loan?
faq.answer: Compare the all-in cost, not just the headline rate: a loan with a low monthly interest but a high management fee can cost more than one with a slightly higher rate and no fee. Shorter tenures usually mean less total interest. Use our loan repayment calculator to estimate the total you'll repay.

title: Best savings accounts in Nigeria (2026)
intro: Savings accounts in Nigeria range from everyday accounts you can dip into anytime to fixed deposits that lock your money for a higher, guaranteed rate. With inflation a real concern, the headline interest rate matters — but so do the conditions: whether interest is paid on every balance or only above a threshold, whether there's a monthly maintenance fee, and how easily you can withdraw. We convert every product to a comparable annual rate and show fees and minimum balances side by side. We list only deposit products from institutions licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria, and we mark which providers are licence-checked and have claimed their listing. Sort by interest rate, fees or minimum balance, and confirm the exact terms with the provider — figures are indicative and change often.

faq.question: How were these savings accounts ranked?
faq.answer: By default we sort by customer rating, with clearly labelled sponsored placements shown first. You can re-sort by highest interest, lowest fees or smallest opening balance. Ranking never affects the licence-verified badge.

faq.question: Is a fixed deposit better than a regular savings account?
faq.answer: Fixed deposits usually pay a higher, guaranteed rate but lock your money for a set term, with a penalty for early withdrawal. Regular savings pay less but let you access funds anytime. Match the choice to when you'll need the money.

faq.question: Are these interest rates guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Savings rates are indicative and can change, and many are tiered by balance. Each product shows when we last verified it. Always confirm with the provider before opening an account.

faq.question: What do I need to open a savings account in Nigeria?
faq.answer: Typically your BVN, a valid ID and a passport photograph; some accounts also ask for a utility bill. Each product lists its required documents.

title: Best business loans in Nigeria (2026)
intro: Business loans in Nigeria run from quick unsecured working-capital facilities to multi-million-naira term loans, asset finance and trade finance. The right option depends on what you're funding (cash-flow gaps, equipment, expansion or imports), how much security you can offer, and your turnover history. Bank SME loans carry the lowest rates but ask for CAC registration, a business account and bank statements; finance companies and microfinance lenders are faster but pricier. We convert every product to a comparable annual basis and show fees alongside the rate, and we list only providers licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria. Sort by interest, fees or amount, and confirm exact terms with the provider before applying — figures are indicative and change often.

faq.question: What do I need to apply for a business loan in Nigeria?
faq.answer: Most lenders require CAC registration, a business bank account, and 6–12 months of bank statements; larger facilities also ask for financial statements and a business plan. Each product lists its required documents.

faq.question: Secured or unsecured?
faq.answer: Smaller working-capital loans may be unsecured; larger term loans, asset finance and trade finance are usually secured against the asset or supported by your turnover. Secured facilities generally carry lower rates.

faq.question: Are these rates guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Business-loan pricing is risk-based and negotiable, so figures are indicative and can change. Each product shows when we last verified it; confirm with the provider.

title: Best credit cards in Nigeria (2026)
intro: Credit cards in Nigeria range from low-fee classic cards to premium cards with airport-lounge access, travel insurance and dollar-spend options. The figures that matter most are the purchase APR (what you pay if you carry a balance), the annual fee, and the interest-free period — pay your statement in full within it and you pay no purchase interest at all. We show the purchase APR on a comparable annual basis next to the annual fee and credit limit, and we list only cards from CBN-licensed banks. Sort by APR or fees, and confirm exact terms with the issuer — figures are indicative and change.

faq.question: How do I avoid paying interest on a credit card?
faq.answer: Pay your full statement balance within the interest-free period (often up to 45 days). You then pay no purchase interest — only the annual fee, if any. Carrying a balance is what triggers the purchase APR.

faq.question: What does the purchase APR mean?
faq.answer: It's the annual interest rate charged on balances you don't pay off in full. Our credit-card cost calculator shows how long a balance takes to clear and the total interest at a given APR and monthly payment.

faq.question: Are these rates and fees guaranteed?
faq.answer: No — they're indicative and can change, and your limit/APR depend on the issuer's assessment. Each card shows when we last verified it; confirm with the bank.

title: Best health insurance (HMO) plans in Nigeria (2026)
intro: Health insurance in Nigeria is mostly sold by HMOs and composite insurers, and plans vary widely on what matters: the annual cover limit, the hospital network, whether out-patient, dental, optical and maternity are included, and how reliably claims are paid. A cheap premium with a tiny limit or a thin network can cost you when you actually need care, so we show the premium, cover limit, any excess and the insurer's claims-paid ratio side by side. We list only insurers and HMOs licensed by NAICOM. Compare the all-in value, check the network and exclusions, and confirm the exact terms with the provider — figures are indicative and change.

faq.question: What should I look at beyond the premium?
faq.answer: The annual cover limit, the hospital network near you, what's included (out-patient, dental, optical, maternity), the excess/co-pay, and the insurer's claims-paid ratio. A low premium with a low limit or weak network is often false economy.

faq.question: What does claims-paid ratio mean?
faq.answer: The share of valid claims the insurer actually pays. Higher is better — it's a practical signal you'll be covered when you need it.

faq.question: Are these premiums guaranteed?
faq.answer: No — premiums are indicative, depend on age/plan/group, and change. Each plan shows when we last verified it; confirm with the provider.

title: Best life insurance in Nigeria (2026)
intro: Life insurance pays a lump sum to your family if you die during the cover period — term life is cheap and pure protection, while whole-life adds a savings/cash-value element at a higher premium. The figures that matter are the cover (sum assured) relative to the premium, the term, and the insurer's claims-paid record. We show premium-from, cover, claims ratio and any conditions side by side, for NAICOM-licensed insurers only. Use our insurance-needs calculator to size your cover, compare the value, and confirm exact terms with the insurer — figures are indicative and change.

faq.question: Term life or whole life?
faq.answer: Term life is cheaper and covers a set period — best for pure protection while you have dependants or debts. Whole life costs more but lasts for life and builds cash value. Match it to your goal.

faq.question: How much cover do I need?
faq.answer: A common rule is enough to replace several years of income plus clear outstanding debts. Our insurance-needs calculator gives a quick estimate.

faq.question: Are premiums guaranteed?
faq.answer: No — they depend on age, health and cover, and are indicative. Each policy shows when we last verified it; confirm with the insurer.

title: Best mutual funds in Nigeria (2026)
intro: Mutual funds let you invest in a professionally managed, diversified portfolio with a low minimum — from equity funds chasing growth to balanced and dollar funds. Returns are not guaranteed and past performance doesn't predict the future, so weigh the fund's risk level, its track record, the management fee and the minimum investment, not just the headline return. We show recent return, risk, minimum and fee side by side, for SEC-registered fund managers only. Use the investment-growth calculator to project outcomes, and confirm exact terms with the manager — figures are indicative and returns can fall as well as rise.

faq.question: Are returns guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Mutual-fund returns vary with the market and can be negative. Treat past performance as context, not a promise, and match the fund's risk level to your horizon.

faq.question: What fees should I check?
faq.answer: The annual management fee is the main one — it compounds over time. Compare it against the fund's risk and track record.

faq.question: How were these ranked?
faq.answer: By default by customer rating, sponsored rows labelled. Re-sort as needed. Ranking is separate from the SEC-registration check.

title: Best money market funds in Nigeria (2026)
intro: Money market funds invest in short-term, low-risk instruments like treasury bills and commercial paper, aiming to preserve capital while paying more than a regular savings account — with daily or near-daily access to your cash. They're a popular place to park naira. The numbers to compare are the recent yield, the management fee and the minimum investment; risk is low but not zero. We show yield, risk, minimum and fee side by side, for SEC-registered managers only. Confirm exact terms with the manager — yields are indicative and move with interest rates.

faq.question: Is a money market fund the same as a savings account?
faq.answer: No — it's an investment, not a deposit, so it isn't a bank account and returns aren't fixed. But it's low-risk and usually pays more than savings, with easy access.

faq.question: Can I lose money?
faq.answer: Losses are rare for money market funds but not impossible; they're low-risk, not no-risk. Yields also move with interest rates.

faq.question: Are yields guaranteed?
faq.answer: No — they're indicative and change. Each fund shows when we last verified it; confirm with the manager.

title: Best pension funds (PFAs) in Nigeria (2026)
intro: Your pension is run by a Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) under the contributory scheme, and you're free to choose or switch yours. Returns differ between PFAs and between the multi-fund types (Fund I–IV, by age/risk appetite), and fees and service quality matter over decades. We show recent return, risk/fund type and the management fee side by side, for PFAs licensed by PenCom only. Use the investment-growth calculator to project your retirement pot, compare PFAs on long-run return and service, and confirm details with the PFA — figures are indicative.

faq.question: Can I change my PFA?
faq.answer: Yes — under PenCom rules you can transfer your Retirement Savings Account between PFAs (typically once a year). Long-run return and service quality are the things to compare.

faq.question: What are Fund I–IV?
faq.answer: The multi-fund structure: more aggressive funds for younger contributors, more conservative ones as you approach retirement. Your age determines the default, and you can opt within limits.

faq.question: Are returns guaranteed?
faq.answer: No — pension returns vary by PFA and fund and are indicative. Confirm with the PFA.

faq.question: Why are some transfers free?
faq.answer: Some fintechs subsidise peer-to-peer transfers within their own network. Bank transfers via NIP usually carry a small regulated fee. Check the fee for the destination you actually use.

faq.question: How fast are transfers?
faq.answer: Local NIP transfers are typically instant. Delays usually come from limits, downtime or compliance checks rather than the rail itself.

title: Cheapest ways to send money to Nigeria (2026)
intro: Sending money to Nigeria from abroad, the headline transfer fee is rarely the real cost — the FX margin (the gap between the rate you get and the mid-market rate) usually matters more. Diaspora-focused apps now offer low or zero fees and tighter margins on the major UK, US, Canada and Europe corridors. We show the fee, FX margin, speed and supported corridors side by side, for CBN-licensed IMTOs and payment providers only. Use our remittance-cost calculator to see what actually arrives, and confirm live rates with the provider — figures are indicative and move constantly.

faq.question: Why compare FX margin, not just the fee?
faq.answer: A 'zero-fee' transfer can still be expensive if the exchange rate is poor. The FX margin is often the bigger cost — our calculator shows the amount that actually arrives after both.

faq.question: Which corridors are covered?
faq.answer: The major diaspora corridors into Nigeria (UK, US, Canada, Europe). Each provider lists the corridors it supports.

faq.question: Are rates guaranteed?
faq.answer: No — fees and FX margins move constantly. Each provider shows when we last verified it; always confirm the live quote before sending.
